Quando competit Actio?
Si dolo malo quis rapuerit. Nam qui aliquo erro-
re ductus, rem suam esse existimans, & imprudens ju-
ris, eo animo rapuerit, quasi domino liceat etiam per
vim rem suam auferre à possessoribus, absolvi debet. §.
ita tamen inst. cod.
Quid Divalibus Constitutionibus
prospectum est?
Ut nemini liceat vi rapere vel rem mobilem, vel se
moventem, licet suam eandem rem existimet: sed si
quis contra statuta principum fecerit, rei quidem
suæ dominio cadat: sin autem aliena res sit, post re-
stitutionem ejus, etiam æstimationem ejusdem rei
præstet. §. ita tamen. inst. cod.
QUIS EST TERTIUS
Titulus?
De Lege Aquilia. Vom Gesetz Aquilia.
Quid constituitur per legem Aquiliam?

l.i: Damni injuriæ actio constituitur per legem A-
quiliam: cujus primo capite cautum est, ut si
quæ pecudum numero sit, injuria occiderit: quanti
ea res in eo anno plurimi fuerit, tantum domino da-
re damnetur. in princ. inst. cod.

main_text.l: Quis intelligitur injuria occidere?
Injuria occidere intelligitur, qui nullo jure occi-
dit. Itaq; qui latronem insidiatorem occiderit, non
tenetur, utiq; si aliter periculum effugere nō potest. §.
injuria autem. inst. cod.

page.notes: The first line of the running head is "IURIS." in spaced capitals. The heading "QUIS EST TERTIUS Titulus?" is set in large italic capitals with a Black-letter-like flourish; the word "Titulus" is italic. "Vom Gesetz Aquilia." is set in Black letter (Fraktur) and is transcribed here in plain text. The Black-letter words are "Vom Gesetz" and the Fraktur "Aquilia" line; the exact Fraktur letterforms are uncertain. The paragraph "Damni injuriæ..." is set in a larger initial D (joined to "Damni"). Some letters in the scan are blurred, notably "Divalibus", "rapere", "æstimationem" and the marginal reference line "M 4"; these should be checked against the original. The "M 4" at the foot is treated as the signature. Show-through and a stray mark near the bottom were ignored.
